verses.1: Then, after some time, an intense, embodied sleep, sent forth by the Lord of the worlds, arose there for Kumbhakarna.
verses.2: Then, Kumbhakarna spoke to his seated brother, saying, "O King, sleep afflicts me; please have a dwelling built for me."
verses.3: Then, artisans like Vishvakarma were appointed by the king to construct a splendid dwelling, one yojana wide and twice that in length.
verses.4: They built for Kumbhakarna a beautiful and unobstructed dwelling, adorned everywhere with variegated pillars of crystal and gold.
verses.5: The structure featured steps made of lapis lazuli, a network of small bells, ivory archways, and platforms of diamond and crystal.
verses.6: The demon (Ravana) had a charming and universally comfortable dwelling built, which was always pleasant, like a sacred cave on Mount Meru.
verses.7: There, the greatly powerful Kumbhakarna, overcome by sleep, remained sleeping for many thousands of years without awakening.
verses.8: When Kumbhakarna was overcome by sleep, the unrestrained Dashanana (Ravana) then indeed killed gods, sages, Yakshas, and Gandharvas.
verses.9: Dashanana (Ravana), having gone to those beautiful gardens, including Nandana and others, very enraged, proceeded to destroy them.
verses.10: The demon destroys everything, playing with rivers like an elephant, throwing down trees like the wind, and shattering mountains like a hurled thunderbolt.
verses.11: Kubera, the lord of wealth and a knower of righteousness, having learned of Daśagrīva's conduct and remembering his own family's appropriate behavior, decided to act.
verses.12: Then, Kubera, wishing to demonstrate brotherly affection and for Daśagrīva's welfare, sent a messenger to Lanka.
verses.13: Having arrived in the city of Lanka, the messenger met Vibhīṣaṇa, who honored him properly and inquired about the purpose of his visit.
verses.14: After inquiring about the welfare of the king and his relatives, Vibhīṣaṇa led the messenger to the assembly hall where Daśānana was seated.
verses.15: Upon seeing the king shining with his own splendor, the messenger honored him with words of "Victory!" and then stood silently.
verses.16: The messenger then spoke words to Dashagriva, who was seated there on an excellent couch adorned with fine coverings.
verses.17: O King, I will tell you everything that your brother spoke, which is befitting of the conduct and lineage of both of us, O hero.
verses.18: Enough of this accumulation of deeds; it is proper that adherence to righteousness be established, if it is possible.
verses.19: I have seen the Nandana garden destroyed, I have heard that sages were killed, and I have heard from you, O King, about the gods' preparations.
verses.20: O lord of Rakshasas, I have been disregarded by you many times, yet one's own relatives, even if they have erred due to childishness, should indeed be cherished.
verses.21: I indeed went to the peak of the Himalayas to practice dharma, having undertaken a severe vow, disciplined and with my senses controlled.
verses.22: There, I saw the Lord, the god Shiva, with the goddess Parvati, and by chance, my left eye fell upon the goddess.
verses.23: I wondered, "Who might this beautiful one be?" and not for any other reason, for Rudra's consort, Parvati, stood there having assumed an incomparable form.
verses.24: By the divine power of the goddess, my left eye was burnt, and it became yellowish-brown, like a flame obscured by dust.
verses.25: Then, I went to another expansive slope of that mountain and silently observed a great vow for eight hundred years.
verses.26: When that austerity was completed, the lord Maheshvara, well pleased, spoke these words there with a gladdened mind.
verses.27: O knower of dharma, O one of good vows, I am indeed pleased by this penance of yours, which resulted in the yellowness (of your eye) from gazing upon the goddess's form.
verses.28: O lord of wealth, this vow has been performed by me and by you alone, for there is no third person who could perform such a vow.
verses.29: This very firm vow was indeed originated by me in the past, therefore, O gentle lord of wealth, desire friendship with me.
verses.30: O sinless one, having been conquered by your penance, become my friend, especially since your left eye was burnt by the power of the goddess.
verses.31: Thus, the name Ekakshipingala will remain eternal, and having obtained friendship and permission from Lord Shankara, Kubera spoke.
verses.32: And having come here, I have heard of this sinful resolve of yours.
verses.33: Therefore, desist from this unrighteous union which disgraces your family, for indeed, the gods along with the groups of sages are contemplating a means to kill you.
verses.34: Thus addressed, Dashagriva, with eyes red with anger, gnashed his teeth and spoke these words.
verses.35: O messenger, I have understood your words which you speak and whose message it is; you are not this person, nor is he the brother by whom you claim to be instigated.
verses.36: This protector of wealth (Kubera) is not speaking what is beneficial for me; rather, this fool is indeed making me hear about his friendship with Maheśvara.
verses.37: O messenger, what you have spoken is not to be forgiven by me, though I have endured his (Kubera's) actions for so long.
verses.38: He (Kubera) thinks that this elder brother, my preceptor, should not be killed by me, but having now heard my words, this decision has been made by me.
verses.39: Relying on the strength of my arms, I shall conquer even the three worlds.
verses.40: Indeed, for the sake of that one (Kubera) alone, I shall, in this very moment, lead those four world-protectors to Yama's abode.
verses.41: Having spoken thus, Ravana, the lord of Lanka, killed the messenger with his sword and gave him to the wicked Rākṣasas to be devoured.
verses.42: Having thus performed auspicious rites and mounted his chariot, Ravana, desirous of conquering the three worlds, went to where Kubera, the lord of wealth, resided. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः ।। 13 ।। Thus ends the thirteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
